name: security-gcp-iap-identity-forwarding-review
intent: Identity-Aware Proxy assertion validation and origin reachability
artifacts: IAP configuration, signed assertion validator, backend ingress and trusted-header usage.
trace: Trace a verified IAP assertion into application identity, including issuer/audience and whether direct origin requests can supply equivalent unverified headers.
experiment: Use an owned proxy/backend fixture; compare intended IAP request and direct synthetic identity-header input.
disproof: An email header name or unreachable origin is not authentication bypass; verify a protected synthetic response under the forged identity.
repair: Validate assertions and origin ingress consistently, preserving authorized proxy traffic and rejecting direct impersonation.
branch_decisions: Check the signed IAP assertion and its exact protected-resource audience; email/identity headers alone may be forgeable on a direct backend path. Determine whether network/ingress restrictions actually prevent that path before declaring bypass. A legitimate request through IAP is a positive control, not proof that all origin routes validate the assertion.
